# Implementation Plan: Image OCR Upload

**Branch**: `001-image-ocr-upload` | **Date**: 2026-05-30 | **Spec**: `specs/001-image-ocr-upload/spec.md`

**Input**: Feature specification from `specs/001-image-ocr-upload/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan is generated by `/speckit.plan` and reflects the current Angular/Nx monorepo architecture.

## Summary

Build an Angular frontend experience in `apps/web` that accepts image uploads via both drag-and-drop and a select-from-device button, validates the file client-side with a 5 MB limit, and sends the image to a new NestJS backend API. The backend will use Google Cloud Vision to detect text and return a structured JSON result that the UI displays immediately.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5.9, Angular 21.2, NestJS compatible with Nx 22.x

**Primary Dependencies**: `@angular/core`, `@angular/forms`, `@nx/angular`, `@nx/nest`, `@nestjs/common`, `@nestjs/platform-express`, `@google-cloud/vision`, `rxjs`

**Storage**: N/A; feature state is transient and held in frontend signal store

**Testing**: `vitest-angular` for frontend unit tests, Cypress for end-to-end flow, NestJS testing module for backend endpoint tests

**Target Platform**: Browser frontend + Node.js backend API

**Project Type**: Web application with backend API

**Performance Goals**: Extracted text returned within 5 seconds for images <= 5 MB; upload feedback displayed immediately

**Constraints**: 5 MB client-side upload limit, allowed MIME types `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/webp`, and secure server-side Google Cloud Vision credential handling

**Scale/Scope**: Single-page OCR upload flow in `apps/web` with a lightweight NestJS API in `apps/api`

## Constitution Check

_GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design._

The feature follows the Literka constitution by keeping reusable UI behavior in `packages/ui`, consuming it from `apps/web`, and isolating backend API logic in a dedicated NestJS app. No constitution violations are identified at this stage.
